author: @liran_tal
reply_text: A Go binary can't run inside a Worker itself, but Cloudflare Containers can run it: package it as a Docker image and have a Worker route the HTTP traffic to it. For the missing auth, Cloudflare's workers-oauth-provider library can sit in that Worker in front of it.

author: @RoundtableSpace
reply_text: Sandboxing fixes what the agent can read. The leak that bites more often is the agent pasting a secret into a prompt, a log or a commit. Pair the sandbox with a hook layer: Agent Guard blocks or masks secrets in Claude Code and Codex, locally, with no telemetry.

author: @marcinperlak
reply_text: Good catch. Rules tied to one tool hold up better inside that tool's own description, right where the agent decides whether to call it. Keep those short too, since some clients clip tool descriptions as well. Server-wide instructions are for the few rules that apply everywhere.

author: @constance_etin
reply_text: Spec-to-MCP is the right starting point. The step people skip is pruning: a big API mapped 1:1 into 80 tools buries the agent in choices. Folding the handful of calls people actually make into a few task-shaped tools usually beats exposing every endpoint.
